title: ID0443499-DC/Si-D/EE-[MP / P0 170001066] - AC1: SECC not longer requires closed contactor: stop charging
description:
Reported behavior/issue: Charging session on AC socket starts and immediatelly stops. MEssage from SECC is
AC1: SECC not longer requires closed contactor: stop charging
User tried multiple times. Screenshot and email can be found from the timeline.
Solution: EV is stopping the session

additional_info.subject: ID0443499-DC/Si-D/EE-[MP / P0 170001066]Charger issue CRM:02681000623
additional_info.body:
Hello colleagues,
Since Markus is out of office, he mentioned to send an email to this recipient.
I have created a ticket to R&D to understand why we are getting this log:
AC1: SECC not longer requires closed contactor: stop charging
The charging session starts succesfully but ends after a few seconds. As soon as I have information, I will convey to you.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0443499-DC/Si-D/EE-[MP / P0 170001066]Charger issue CRM:02681000623
additional_info.body:
Hi Markus,
We checked this ticket with R&D and the answer they provided was that the EV should be the one requesting the stop since the PilotState C to B comes at the same time as the message:
AC1: SECC not longer requires closed contactor: stop charging
As such, I checked the logs from the past 4 weeks and not all the sessions are interrupted which means that it's most likely R&D's scenario. Since we don't have EcoG logs for this, I don't know how we can test it besides going on site and measure CP while it's charging.
R&D's reply:
"T
here is a control bit tranfered from the SECC to the PLC to close the contactor. during charging it is expected, that this control bit is high. whenever the SECC does not longer request the PLC to close the contactor, the statemachine performs a transition to the next state, which is "STOP_CHARGE_AND_UNLOCK_SOCKET". W
hat is interesting here, is the fact, that we do not get any additional information, why the SECC changed the control bit to false. I
t could be possible, that the EV triggered it, because we see the Pilotstate changing from C2 to B2 nearly at the same time and Pilotstate B2 does not longer require a closed contactor. I
f the charger would have triggered the session stop, it would be more likely, that the Pilotstate change from C2 to C1 (PWM turned off) (or to B1, in case the EV opened switch S2)"
What do you think?
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco
